highlights.text: New sounds for water, the well and moving parts
Turn photos get a polaroid and survive the app closing
Chapters open faster
Spirits breathe and glance around while they wait

paragraphs.text: After You has new sounds. Footsteps sound on Home, with birds in the background, and bells have a real ring that other sounds don't cut short. A reel turns while the Wishing Well's bucket and ladder, the First Steps lift and the bridges move, and dropping down in the Wishing Well ends in a soft plunk. Turn of the Tide has lapping water and a rush as the water rises or falls. In the second turn, the memory's levers and switches make their sounds too.

When your spirit finishes before the memory does, it dozes by the goal while the camera follows the memory. A row under the chapter name shows who you're waiting for, and you can hold Fast-forward or tap Skip to end. A bell or beacon you reached first rings when the memory arrives. Resting spirits breathe now and glance around when they're alone, on the ready and waiting cards too. Speech bubbles on levers bob gently unless Reduce motion is on.

The optional turn photo has a new polaroid card, with the date written by hand along the bottom, like 15th Oct '26. If Android closed After You while the camera was open, you could land on Home with your turn saved and no photo. Now the photo is kept: Home says it's waiting, and Open room takes you back to send it with that turn.

Chapters open faster. They no longer wait for Home to finish checking your keepsakes, and every chapter builds behind the opening card straight to the stage you're on. Paid chapters open behind that one card too, without a checking card first. Enter the Lighthouse in the store now opens the six-stage Lighthouse, like its chapter card does.

Rooms cope better with quick taps. If the room hub is busy when you tap Continue, Open or Host, it shows Opening room and carries on. Begin and Resume stay live while a room refreshes, and a finished room's replay opens straight away. Your rooms loads faster, and a room that fails to load shows as unavailable instead of failing the whole list. Hosting or joining at the room limit now says so. Finished and closed rooms no longer count toward the 20 rooms you can have in play.
If Android backup is on, it now copies your solo progress and saved replays to your Google account, but only when the copy is encrypted with your phone's screen lock. Photos aren't included.

What's new is a button on Home, with a dot after an update, and See all changes opens the notes for every version on GitHub. Android Back now presses each screen's own way back and closes an open card first. Surfaces that flickered are fixed in several chapters, including the Wishing Well's rim and the Lighthouse's lens posts.

highlights.text: Easier on your phone, so it stays cooler
Taps in lists work the first time
Rooms with a friend recover when something fails
The spirit's shadow stops flickering

paragraphs.text: After You asks less of your phone now, to help it stay cooler. Play runs at up to 60 frames a second. Menus and cards draw at most 30 a second, and only when something changes, then go back to full speed as soon as you touch the screen. The 3D view is drawn at most 720 lines tall on Low and 1080 on Balanced. Once a chapter loads, its fixed scenery is folded into a few large pieces, so your phone draws far fewer of them every frame.
To play at your screen's full refresh rate, turn on Unlimited frame rate on the Graphics page. It uses more battery and can warm your phone.

Taps in lists work the first time, even if your finger moves a little while you press. Join on the Friends page stays live while the list refreshes, and a tap made during the refresh goes through once it lands.

Playing with a friend copes better when something goes wrong. A room your friend closed shows as closed in the room hub, and a turn sent to it moves into the room's history instead of holding up your other rooms. If the reply to a saved turn is lost, the game checks with the server and sends the turn again. A room the server refused for good no longer blocks the rest, and after a restart the hub reads the chapter list before it opens a room, so that room's turn can be saved. You also get a notification when your friend closes a room.
Play with a friend keeps the chapter you picked after you visit Friends or a room, so it doesn't fall back to First Steps anymore. Each room in the hub is named after its own chapter.
Watch replay opens the room you tapped it in, and saves a finished room's replay first if it needs to. Android Back now leaves Together replays the same way their Back button does.

highlights.text: Sleeping Lighthouse is one chapter you can host online
Smoother play, without the pause after a turn
Finished rooms stay in Your rooms
Friends show by the nickname you gave them

paragraphs.text: The Sleeping Lighthouse is now one six-stage chapter, and you can play it solo or host it for a friend online. Hosting it needs Full Journey, and your friend can join without buying anything. Your solo Lighthouse progress carries over the first time you open the new chapter. Each Lighthouse place also has a together keepsake now, so Home has 64 keepsakes in all.

The game runs much more smoothly. Long attempts no longer stutter as the turn grows, and the pauses at the end of a turn, when you leave Home and when you reopen a finished chapter are gone. Chapters build over several frames behind the opening card while the loading bar keeps moving, and Home stops drawing its island behind Friends and other full pages.

Finished rooms show up properly in Your rooms. Each one stays in the list with its chapter after you both save the replay, and Watch replay clears its dot. A shared replay lists every part when it opens, rooms show when they last changed, and the newest room comes first. Your friend's turn photos download into a shared replay by themselves.
Friends appear by the nickname you gave them, or as "a friend", on room cards, on the waiting card and in shared replays, never by a raw id.
Play with a friend doesn't get stuck anymore when your last room's replay has moved to your phones or the room is gone. Joining from the room hub by typing a room code works now.

Hosting alerts were fixed. A room you host for Friends is shared as soon as you host it, the alert is kept if the app restarts, and it is sent again if the first try fails. Alerts stay on after a cold start, and after a reinstall the game asks once for notification permission. A friend's hosting alert also shows inside the app while it's open.

Speech bubbles slide beside a spirit instead of covering it, and every lever bubble points at the top of the knob. Balanced and High graphics don't draw shadows now, and the lighting is as bright as before. In Explore on Home, the bridge rises as you walk up to it, and the keepsake arrows are hidden.

highlights.text: Two free chapters: The Wishing Well and Turn of the Tide
Long Way Home has a harder finale
Keepsakes stand on the home island
Full Journey is a monthly or yearly subscription

paragraphs.text: There are two new free chapters, The Wishing Well and Turn of the Tide, and you can play them solo or host them for a friend online. Long Way Home has a new version with a harder finale and three ways through. It keeps the house and the first stage, and keepsakes you already earned there still count. To join a room in any of these chapters, your friend needs 0.6.0 too.

Full Journey is now a subscription, paid monthly or yearly. It pays for hosting and server costs, and it unlocks the paid chapters for solo play and for hosting a friend. If you bought Full Journey before, it stays unlocked.

Keepsakes now stand on the home island as landmarks on their own bridged islands. Each one shows whether you finished its chapter solo, with a friend, or both. Tap Explore on Home to walk a spirit around them.

The seed looks like the white seed on the app icon now, and it tumbles as it flies. The turn timer is a small seed that moves along a dotted path to a sprout. In Long Way Home and Turn of the Tide, lever and pad labels are speech bubbles that point at their control. Most chapters have new scenery, and the chapter pictures were retaken to match.

A loading card shows while a chapter opens, and solo chapters open faster because the game reuses checks it already made on your phone. Sound pitch slides smoothly within a range, and the same moment plays at the same pitch in replays. The ball and the seed share one motion blur, which fixes the thin strips behind the ball in Rolling Home.

Play Solo and Play with a friend use the same chapter picker. You can close a room that is still in play, and remove finished or closed rooms from your list. The old Play together screen is gone, so Back from hosting returns to Play with a friend. Notify for a friend stays on after you leave Friends and come back.

Replays shows the whole list as soon as it opens, and you can tap anywhere on a row to select it. Sleeping Lighthouse solo replays open from the Solo replays list. Most solo chapters have a Redo my previous turn button, and Notifications has a switch that alerts you when your friend asks for a redo.

highlights.text: Invite a friend with a link
Codes start with friend- or room-
Home has a new layout
Replays open faster after a restart

paragraphs.text: You can send invite links now. Tap Share Invite on Friends or on Home to send your friend a link. If your friend has After You on an Android phone, the link opens the game and asks them to confirm adding you. A friend who doesn't have the game yet sees a page with your friend code and a Google Play button.
paragraphs.ios_text: You can send invite links now. Tap Share Invite on Friends or on Home to send your friend a link.

paragraphs.text: Codes now say what they are: friend codes start with friend- and room codes start with room-. Older codes still work. Your friends need this version to use the new codes and links.

Home has a new layout. Play with your friend is at the top, Play Solo and Friends sit side by side, and Replays and Invite your friends come after them. Settings is the gear icon in the top corner. The keepsakes box shows the keepsakes you still have to earn.
Play Solo has big play buttons on each chapter card. Finished chapters have a tick and a different colour, and locked Full Journey chapters are darker and carry a lock.
Replays shows a loading bar while it loads, instead of an empty list. It also remembers which replays it has already checked, so the list opens much faster after you restart the game.
On Friends, Copy is a single icon next to Share Invite. Tap a friend's code to copy it.

highlights.text: Chapters are picture cards you tap to play
Your level stays on screen after a turn
Lists and dropdowns scroll when you drag them
Footsteps and catches change pitch

paragraphs.text: Each chapter is a card with its picture on it. Tap a card to play it alone, and a check mark shows which chapters you've finished. Free chapters come first, and playing with a friend starts at Play with your friend. The hosting page for a locked chapter shows its picture next to the unlock options.

When you finish a turn, the level stays on screen next to a side panel. The panel says your turn is saved, shows whose turn is next and has one button for turning on notifications. Other actions, like asking for a redo or reporting a player, are in Room options. The invitation code has a full-size Copy button that confirms when it worked, and the code goes away once your friend joins.

In Play with a friend, Your rooms scroll in their own column, the buttons line up, each room shows its status in a small tag, and Join stays off until you enter a code. On Friends, Notify sits next to Join and is easy to see when it's on, and your code has Share code and Copy buttons. Lists and dropdowns, such as the chapter picker and Account & recovery, scroll when you drag them.

In Replays the preview stays in view while the list scrolls, and the Earlier islands have new pictures. Tap either character on Home to watch them celebrate, and they close their eyes happily when they meet. Footsteps, catches and meetups change pitch, so they don't sound the same every time. There's also a new line at the bottom of Home.

Changing a friend's nickname, turning on hosting alerts and answering a redo request happen in matching in-game popups, and a popup tells you when a friend asks you to redo your turn.

Replays has a list next to a large preview, and Together opens straight into your most recent room, with a picker for your other rooms. The room hub shows the right chapter names and pictures, the waiting panel shows who's next, and First Steps, High and Low and Relay Isles have new pictures.
